name: DeepL Pro
tagline: Connect a local translation memory editor to a user-supplied model API

pricing.basis: annual billing, per user per month
pricing.notes: Typical Starter monthly user price; regional currency and character charges can differ.

tiers.name: DeepL Account (Free)
tiers.limits: Web/desktop translation with limits; files up to 5MB and 100,000 characters; 1 image translation/month; Microsoft Word add-in caps Translator at 3,000 characters/day and Write at 2,000/day
tiers.notes: DeepL does not publish one universal monthly text-character cap for every free surface; limits differ by product interface.

tiers.name: Individual
tiers.limits: 1 user; professional translation; files up to 30MB and 1M characters each for DOCX/PPTX/PDF; some formats unavailable
tiers.notes: Billed annually; current public page did not expose a month-to-month US rate.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: Team controls; files up to 30MB and 1M characters each; XLSX/XLIFF/IDML supported; additional file packs available
tiers.notes: Billed annually; current public page did not expose a month-to-month US rate.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Business administration and security; files up to 100MB and 1M characters each; additional file packs available
tiers.notes: Billed annually; current public page did not expose a month-to-month US rate.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom users, controls, translation volume, and support

pricing.freeTierCaps: Free account: files up to 5MB/100,000 characters, 1 image translation/month; Word add-in 3,000 Translator characters/day and 2,000 Write characters/day; no single universal text cap published
pricing.billingTerms: Individual, Team, and Business prices shown per user/month billed annually; Enterprise custom; taxes may apply
pricing.hiddenCosts: Translator subscriptions do not include API access; API Developer/Growth/Enterprise are separate products with character/audio quotas and overages. Team/Business can buy 50 extra file translations per seat, those add-ons renew monthly, and unused file translations do not roll over.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For DeepL Pro, connect a local translation memory editor to a user-supplied model API. The hard boundary is deepl's proprietary translation model, document handling, privacy operations, and language quality, plus translation memory, collaboration, and deployment integrations.
coreLoopDIY: Connect a local translation memory editor to a user-supplied model API, preserve context, review translations, import and export standard files, and publish approved strings.
requirements: optional DeepL or OpenAI API key
whatYouLose: DeepL's proprietary translation model, document handling, privacy operations, and language quality
moatNotes: translation memory, collaboration, and deployment integrations
ongoingBurden: file formats, placeholders, plural rules, screenshots, context, permissions, review, glossary, machine translation, sync, and backups
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for DeepL Pro because localization teams pay because language context, review discipline, translators, and release integrations are the hard parts. The recurring cost buys file formats, placeholders, plural rules, screenshots, context, permissions, review, glossary, machine translation, sync, and backups, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Tolgee
priorArt.desc: Active open-source localization platform with translation memory and in-context tooling.

alternatives.name: OmegaT
alternatives.desc: A desktop translation-memory workbench that can call your chosen machine-translation provider and keeps the project local.

alternatives.name: MateCat
alternatives.desc: A free hosted CAT editor with translation memory and machine translation; use your own judgment where DeepL sold confidence.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Swordfish
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The source is open, but the ready-made installers are a 30-day trial, so a non-builder has not escaped the meter.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a small-team string-management system DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for DeepL Pro in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and one optional machine-translation API; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: connect a local translation memory editor to a user-supplied model API, preserve context, review translations, import and export standard files, and publish approved strings.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement projects, locales, keys, namespaces, descriptions, screenshots, translations, and review status.
Import and export JSON, YAML, PO, and XLIFF while preserving placeholders and plural forms.
Add glossary checks, missing-string filters, translation memory, comments, and reviewer assignment.
Use machine translation only on selected strings and show provider, cost, and source text before approval.
Provide token-authenticated pull and push endpoints for CI with an immutable change log.
Add backups, locale deletion safeguards, and a pseudo-localization preview.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out a translator labor marketplace.
Deliberately leave out a global website translation proxy.
Deliberately leave out enterprise integrations, legal translation assurance, and round-the-clock support.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
